There have been no bankruptcy filings or imminent defaults as of early 2026, tempering the 74% forecast.

justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.74 to 0.46 due to credible near-term liquidity cushion (cash and revolver), absence of imminent default signals, and the qualitative note that Altman Z-score and industry headwinds alone do not deterministically imply an imminent bankruptcy filing before May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Altman Z-score distress signal
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier's Altman Z-score is around 0.37–0.38, placing it in the distress zone and implying a meaningful bankruptcy risk within the next two years (Altman framework; GuruFocus data as of February 2026).

causal-factors.name: Near-term debt maturities
causal-factors.rationale: Future debt principal payments include about $209 million remaining in 2025 and $120 million in 2026 (total $512 million through 2029), which adds refinancing pressure despite current liquidity (SEC 10-Q as of 3/31/2025).

causal-factors.name: Industry-wide distress environment
causal-factors.rationale: PwC's 2026 restructuring outlook signals higher bankruptcy activity; CreditRiskMonitor's FRISK index remained in high-risk territory around 1.3% in 2026, indicating elevated sector risk (PwC 2026 outlook; CreditRiskMonitor FRISK data).

causal-factors.name: Liquidity cushion and near-term liquidity
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier reported roughly $889 million of total liquidity and an undrawn $205 million revolving facility as of early 2025, providing a cushion to meet 12-month cash needs (SEC 2025 10-Q; Frontier press materials).

causal-factors.name: Sector/M&A context with Spirit Airlines
causal-factors.rationale: Spirit’s standalone recapitalization and Frontier’s repeated takeover proposals amid Spirit’s restructuring signal ongoing sector stress and regulatory/valuation headwinds for ULCCs (AP/Reuters coverage and Spirit Frontier disclosures).

causal-factors.name: Frontier Altman Z-Score distressed indicator
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier's Z-score (~0.38) places it in the distress zone (Z <= 1.8), and distressed-zone firms historically have bankruptcy probabilities >80% over the next two years (source: GuruFocus ULCC Z-score page, Feb 2026).

causal-factors.name: Industry-wide distress and rising bankruptcy risk in US corporates
causal-factors.rationale: US corporate bankruptcies rose in 2025 with indicators such as a FRISK index around 1%, and the pace through Q1 2025 was the fastest since 2010, increasing baseline risk for leveraged airlines (sources: CreditRiskMonitor article; Bloomberg report).

causal-factors.name: Frontier's near-term liquidity cushion despite debt maturities
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 31, 2025 Frontier had about $686 million in cash and current debt maturities of $263 million, plus an undrawn revolver (e.g., $205 million; potentially up to $500 million), providing a cushion against near-term bankruptcy risk (sources: Frontier 10-Q FRON-20250331; Revolver-related reporting).

causal-factors.name: Frontier's failed Spirit merger reduces rescue options
causal-factors.rationale: Spirit Airlines rejected Frontier's takeover offer, removing a potential strategic rescue or financing channel and increasing distress risk if no alternative relief emerges (sources: Spirit press release Feb 11, 2025; Bloomberg Jan 29, 2025).

causal-factors.name: Liquidity cushion and undrawn revolver
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier reported substantial liquidity (roughly $889 million) including a $686 million cash balance and an undrawn revolver potentially up to $500 million, supporting near-term obligations through 2029 and reducing bankruptcy risk before May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Altman Z-score in distress zone
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier's Altman Z-score was 0.38 (Feb 2026), placing it in the distress zone and associated with a bankruptcy probability within two years according to Altman’s framework.

causal-factors.name: Near-term debt maturities and liquidity buffer
causal-factors.rationale: Debt principal payments of about $209 million in 2025 remainder and $120 million in 2026 are sizable but manageable given strong liquidity, reducing near-term default risk unless liquidity deteriorates.

causal-factors.name: Industry-wide distress risk rising in 2026
causal-factors.rationale: PwC’s 2026 restructuring outlook and higher baseline bankruptcy activity suggest elevated sector risk for leveraged carriers, increasing the probability of distress signals for Frontier.

causal-factors.name: Absence of bankruptcy filing signals as of Mar 1, 2026
causal-factors.rationale: No bankruptcy filing by Frontier was reported by that date, which lowers the probability modestly, though distress indicators remain non-negligible.

synthesis: The objections reveal credible near-term liquidity cushions and absence of acute distress signals, warranting a downward calibration from 74%. Given persistent distress indicators and sector risk, but solid liquidity and no imminent filing, a calibrated probability around 0.46 with a plausible 0.34–0.58 range is justified.
